title: The reverend Hugh C. Love
html_source: Reverend Love appears with Ned Lambert and J. J. O'Molloy when they show him the ancient council chamber of St. Mary’s Abbey. He is writing a book on Irish history and is preoccupied by the Fitzgerald family. Mark Osteen, in “The Economy of Ulysses” pg. 197 writes: “And like Haines, who also appropriates things Irish for English use, Love is at first invisible, entering the text merely as a ‘refined accent;’… Love’s expropriation of history also links him to that other Unionist, Garrett Deasy: Love says he ‘won’t trespass on your valuable time;” Deasy asks to 'trespass on your valuable space.’ But as Anglo-Protestant usurpers, they cannot help but be trespassers."
